blueprint.background: Fictional 47-year-old man, never smoker, reflux symptoms and newly confirmed hypertension.
blueprint.presenting_complaint: Cough already present January 8; progressively limiting through July.
blueprint.working_diagnosis: Initial reflux/post-viral possibility; later ACE inhibitor contribution, reflux and anxiety considered.
blueprint.medication_timeline: Lisinopril ordered February 12, intended February 13; use reported March 19 and July 8. Stop July 8; losartan thereafter by patient report. No administration proof.
blueprint.laboratory_trend: CRP 4, 12, 18, 31, 28 mg/L; HGB 14.1, 13.6, 13.1, 12.4, 12.5 g/dL. Nonspecific; no etiologic diagnosis.
blueprint.imaging: Right basal opacity March 19, persistent April 30 and July 8. CT booked July 29, beyond dataset cutoff.
blueprint.follow_up: April 30 repeat imaging completed even though scheduling task still outstanding; report not yet finalized at scheduling review.
blueprint.turning_point: July 8 symptom progression, weight loss and unresolved focal opacity prompt expedited referral.
blueprint.ground_truth_interpretation: June history conflicts with contemporaneous January and March symptom records. Cough predates lisinopril prescription; medication contribution to persistence is still possible. Underlying etiology is unresolved. No proven malpractice, malignancy, infection or causal harm.

expected_findings.expected_claim: June consultation states cough first began May 26 with none before; contemporaneous January 8 and March 19 records establish earlier cough, including before lisinopril was prescribed.

anchors.quote: Cough present for about ten days
Cough first began on May 26, 2026; no cough before then.

expected_findings.counterevidence: June note may reflect erroneous or incomplete history; no proven deliberate action. January and March documentation are contemporaneous, not late July entries. No documented full resolution between visits.

expected_non_findings.claim: Repeat April radiograph was never performed
expected_non_findings.reason: Scheduling task reviewed at 11:00 before report finalized at 12:00; imaging performed at 10:00. Status lag is not evidence of absent care.

expected_non_findings.claim: Lisinopril definitively caused or cannot contribute to cough
expected_non_findings.reason: Earlier cough challenges sole-onset attribution; contribution remains uncertain. Two-week withdrawal interval is inconclusive.

expected_non_findings.claim: GERD or anxiety alone explains deterioration, or opacity establishes cancer/infection
expected_non_findings.reason: Reflux improved but cough persisted; opacity and inflammatory markers nonspecific. CT, spirometry and pathology unavailable.

evaluation_criteria: Resolve all decisive IDs and exact quote anchors
Compare original event and documentation times
Do not infer unrecorded care or a final diagnosis
acceptable_uncertainty: Underlying cause of opacity and inflammatory trend
clinical_review: Pending independent expert review; automated consistency checks do not establish clinical accuracy.
